summary: Summarizes OAM tools defined in the IETF for IP unicast, MPLS, MPLS-TP, pseudowires, and TRILL. The focus is on detecting and isolating failures and on performance monitoring. It can serve as an index to the main OAM tools.

eli5.summary: This is a catalogue of tools that check whether a network is healthy and find out where it is broken.

questions: overview of oam in mpls and ip
how do you detect network failures
subtitle: A catalog of tools for detecting failures and measuring performance in networks

tldr.problem: Networks require tools to detect and isolate failures quickly and measure performance. Different network layers and technologies use different OAM protocols, creating fragmentation and complexity.
tldr.mechanism: The IETF has defined OAM tools for each network layer: IP ping and traceroute for IP networks, BFD for generic failure detection, LSP Ping for MPLS label-switched paths, MPLS-TP OAM for transport networks, and OWAMP/TWAMP for precise performance measurement.
tldr.outcome: Operators now have a comprehensive toolkit for network monitoring across IP, MPLS, MPLS-TP, pseudowires, and TRILL, enabling multi-layer OAM strategies that monitor both data and label planes independently.

facts.label: Primary OAM functions
facts.value: 3: connectivity verification, path discovery, performance monitoring

today: RFC 7276 remains a comprehensive index to IETF OAM tools published as of June 2014. These tools continue to be foundational for network operations, enabling multi-layer monitoring strategies that detect failures quickly and measure performance accurately across diverse network technologies.

sections.title: Network Operations and Monitoring Fundamentals
sections.content:
Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) is a toolset for fault detection and isolation, and for performance measurement. OAM functions detect failures early (ideally before users are affected), track resource usage, and facilitate repairs and upgrades. Historically, OAM originated in circuit-switched technologies like E1, T1, PDH, and SONET/SDH, where it was essential for carrier-grade reliability. As packet-based networks evolved to carry critical telephony and data services, they needed similar OAM sophistication beyond basic mechanisms like ICMP ping and router hellos.

Modern networks use multi-layer OAM: each network layer has its own OAM protocols, from IP to MPLS to pseudowires to application services. For example, IP OAM monitors the customer-level end-to-end path while MPLS OAM monitors the provider-level connection underneath. OAM tools operate in either proactive mode (sending messages periodically to detect failures before users notice) or on-demand mode (activated manually when investigating anomalies).
sections.eli5: Networks need ways to constantly check that everything is working, or to debug when something breaks. Since networks are made of layers, you need different checking tools for each layer.

sections.title: OAM Concepts and Categories
sections.content:
OAM has three key concepts: Connectivity Verification allows a node to verify that it is connected to a destination and that the connection path is correct. Continuity Checks verify that a destination is reachable, typically sent proactively to detect interruptions. Together they form complementary mechanisms often used in conjunction.

OAM tools fall into two broad categories by connection model: connection-oriented tools (like MPLS LSP Ping) monitor a specific labeled path through the network, while connectionless tools (like IP Ping) test reachability without defining a specific connection. OAM tools are built on OAM functions (atomic measurement types like connectivity verification or path discovery) and implemented through OAM protocols (specific message formats and procedures).

The three primary OAM functions are: (1) Connectivity Verification and Continuity Checks, (2) Path Discovery and Fault Localization to identify where failures occur, and (3) Performance Monitoring including Loss Measurement and Delay Measurement to track packet loss rates and latency.
sections.eli5: OAM tools check if you can reach a destination, find out which hop is broken, and measure delays. Some tools watch constantly, others check only when you ask.

sections.title: Basic IP and Bidirectional Tools
sections.content:
IP Ping (defined in [ICMPv4] and [ICMPv6]) uses ICMP Echo requests to test IP reachability. An originator sends an ICMP Echo request and waits for a reply from the destination. This serves as a single-ended continuity check; both directions must be tested separately. Ping can target unicast or multicast addresses, though ICMP filtering on some routers limits its usefulness on the public Internet.

IP Traceroute discovers the path between source and destination by sending UDP (or ICMP or TCP) packets with incrementing Time-To-Live values. Each router along the path returns ICMP Time Exceeded messages, revealing the route hop by hop. Traceroute shows latency at each hop and identifies where paths diverge. A variant called Paris Traceroute discovers multiple available paths (ECMP) by varying header fields.

Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) is a generic OAM tool deployed over various encapsulating protocols (IP, MPLS LSPs, pseudowires). BFD provides rapid failure detection: it maintains bidirectional sessions and declares a session Down when expected control packets are not received within the Detection Time (calculated from transmission rate and a configurable Detect Mult parameter). BFD runs in asynchronous (proactive) mode or demand mode, and includes an Echo function for loopback testing.
sections.eli5: Ping is like shouting 'hello?' and waiting to hear back. Traceroute traces the path that a packet takes to the destination by getting responses from each hop. BFD is a quick way to detect when a connection breaks.

sections.title: MPLS and Transport-Specific Monitoring
sections.content:
LSP Ping is the IETF's OAM tool for MPLS Label Switched Paths. Operating in Ping mode, it verifies end-to-end connectivity between Label Edge Routers. In Traceroute mode, it enables hop-by-hop fault isolation using the TTL field to progressively identify the sub-path where failures occur. LSP Ping verifies data-plane vs. control-plane consistency and detects MTU problems. It handles Equal-Cost Multipath (ECMP) by monitoring different Forwarding Equivalence Classes to test all available paths.

MPLS-TP OAM extends OAM for MPLS Transport Profile (used in carrier transport networks). It defines Maintenance Entities (ME) as the units monitored and Maintenance Points (MEP at endpoints, MIP at intermediate nodes) as the monitoring locations. The MPLS-TP OAM toolset includes Continuity Check and Connectivity Verification, Route Tracing (similar to traceroute), Lock Instruct (taken a path out of service), Alarm Reporting, Remote Defect Indication (RDI), and Performance Monitoring for Loss Measurement and Delay Measurement.

Pseudowire OAM monitors emulated circuits carried over MPLS. It uses Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification (VCCV) or Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh) to carry OAM messages in-band with the data traffic, ensuring OAM packets experience the same treatment as user traffic.
sections.eli5: MPLS networks need special OAM tools because they use labels instead of IP addresses. MPLS-TP is for service provider networks and has more advanced monitoring. Pseudowires need to check that emulated circuits are working.

sections.title: Performance Measurement and Active Testing
sections.content:
OWAMP (One-Way Active Measurement Protocol) and TWAMP (Two-Way Active Measurement Protocol) are precision measurement tools. OWAMP measures one-way loss and delay from a sender to a receiver using synchronized clocks. TWAMP adds a return path for two-way measurement and does not require synchronized clocks between endpoints. These protocols are more accurate than ICMP-based measurements and are used for Service Level Agreement (SLA) monitoring and network performance analytics.

Loss Measurement (LM) in MPLS-TP and other protocols counts transmitted and received packets to calculate packet loss rates over monitored connections. Delay Measurement (DM) monitors round-trip delay and delay variation (jitter). These measurements can be performed proactively at regular intervals or on-demand when investigating service issues. Measurement accuracy depends on fate-sharing: OAM traffic must take the same paths and receive the same treatment as the data traffic it monitors.
sections.eli5: Performance monitoring tools count how many packets are lost and how much delay there is. Some tools send their own test packets, others watch real traffic. They help you know if your network is delivering good quality.

sections.title: Deployment Across Network Layers and Technologies
sections.content:
The choice of OAM tools depends on the network technology and deployment scenario. IP networks use Ping and Traceroute for basic troubleshooting and BFD for fast failure detection. MPLS networks use LSP Ping for path monitoring and BFD for link monitoring. Service provider transport networks use MPLS-TP OAM for management-plane monitoring and performance tracking. Pseudowires use VCCV to carry OAM messages inline with emulated traffic.

TRILL OAM (Transparent Interconnection of Lots of Links) is defined for campus Ethernet switching with TRILL encapsulation. Multi-layer OAM strategies allow different tools to monitor different layers independently: customer-level IP OAM validates the application view while provider-level MPLS OAM monitors the underlying infrastructure. This layered approach enables operators to isolate problems to specific network segments.

Equipment vendors should implement OAM tools as standard capabilities to enable early fault detection, rapid service restoration, and accurate performance reporting. The availability of comprehensive OAM toolsets is essential for operating carrier-grade networks that support critical services.
sections.eli5: You pick different OAM tools depending on what kind of network you have. For IP, you use Ping. For MPLS, you use LSP Ping. For service provider networks, you use MPLS-TP OAM. They all fit together to give you complete visibility.
